correctness.rationale: An idempotent fixes its whole image. A singleton can map only to a singleton; a free orbit may collapse to a singleton in one way or map to a prescribed free orbit by any of q right translations. This gives precisely the two types of rooted components and the rank k+qℓ. Conjugacy by coordinate right translations changes a satellite-to-root phase h_i to s_i^(-1) h_i s_root. Set root translations to the identity and choose s_i=h_i independently on the satellites: there is no residual nonabelian invariant. Orbit permutations then identify exactly the equal multisets. Labeling the rooted stars gives denominators (s−1)!t!, (c−1)!, and the two multiplicity factorials; restoring a choice of q phases per free satellite of a free root gives (1). The independent multiset factors give (2)–(3), and choosing image roots first yields (4), including 0^0=1. At a=b=2 there are nine profiles and (4) gives 6q+17. Using G^op for the regular-orbit translation group yields the same wreath product up to isomorphism via inversion. The phrase 'does depend on q' describes the general labeled formula, not every parameter choice: labeled counts are q-independent for b≤1 and strictly q-dependent for b≥2. The frozen nonabelian finite tests are corroboration, not the proof; the uploaded code was not executed.
residual_risks: Partial maps or intermediate stabilizers require different arguments.
Individual orbit sizes need not vary with q if there are no free-to-free satellite phases; this does not alter the formula.

evidence: 14319157d092 classifies partial idempotents while fixing each distinguished point individually. Here the trivial points can permute, the maps are total, and phases act on regular orbits.
3aa290484152 has a similar phase normalization and orbit-size expression for rooted forests of nilpotent maps with one fixed point; a nilpotent idempotent in that setting is zero.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The shared rooted-component mechanism is not itself new. Neither changing from nilpotence to idempotence nor from individually fixed distinguished points to a permutable singleton species with regular orbits is a parameter substitution in those conclusions. The mixed profile census and its rank and weight data remain distinct.

evidence: The partition-average proof in 46b24971b86b includes the ordinary S_n-conjugacy profile by fiber sizes, not just a labeled centralizer count.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Ordinary or homogeneous fibers do not distinguish the two possible root species and the two supplier species at a singleton root. The labeled count alone does not give a unit-orbit size or class count.

evidence: The indexed exact formulas found apply to labeled permutation-centralizer counts, partial-map unit classes with named fixed points, or nilpotent equivariant-map classes with one fixed point. The inspected passages do not tabulate (1)–(3) for this mixed total-idempotent regime.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Counts for another action or another equation on the maps do not determine the class census. An exact match would need both singleton and regular roots, the stated unit action and rank in image points.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the complete mixed fixed/free classification together with the exact individual orbit sizes and rank-refined class product. The general endomorphism framework, ordinary fiber-size profiles, homogeneous phase normalization and homogeneous labeled count are established precedents, not additional novelty. The closest mixed-isotropy and partial-map analogues do not yield this total-idempotent census.
residual_risks: An uninspected general theorem on G-set retraction isomorphism or orbit-size enumeration could subsume part of the profile argument; the full rank and orbit-size census is not claimed to have certified priority.
Chronology is unresolved for the distinct same-day analogues.

value.rationale: The two natural stabilizer extremes in one finite G-set give a complete classification, including the size of every individual unit class and point-rank distribution. The exact separation between group-independent class multiplicities and group-order-dependent labeled weights is useful for enumeration and is not supplied by the known homogeneous labeled count alone.
residual_risks: Value is attached to the mixed census, not to general priority for rooted stars, phase normalization, or arbitrary G-set stabilizers.
